motivation: After static geometry, annual neighborhood state, depth/sediment and a bulk benthic-light proxy failed to explain Tampa annual condition, test the published Tampa Bay compound hot-fresh stress hypothesis against Thalassia plant-condition states.

published_source.article: Beck et al. 2024, Estuaries and Coasts, Hot and Fresh
published_source.provenance_note: The source artifact was generated from station-specific GAM daily predictions and aligned to Tampa Bay transect survey intervals in the published analysis code.

exposure_definition.exact_code_relation: temp daily prediction >= 30 C AND salinity daily prediction <= 25 ppt
exposure_definition.station_interval_metric: maximum consecutive daily run with both thresholds true within each published transect interval
exposure_definition.segment_interval_metric: mean station-level maximum run within bay segment and transect year

next_gate: If the published compound-stress exposure passes coverage, freeze a fixed-transect Thalassia plant-condition analysis before opening focal response.
claim_boundary: The daily stress sequence is model-derived from monthly EPC observations, not direct daily measurement.
The original published reconstruction used the full environmental time series; any downstream Tampa analysis is retrospective ecological association/prediction, not prospective climate forecasting.
Thresholds were partly chosen in the published study for statistical utility and are stress indices, not proven physiological limits.
No focal Thalassia response is opened in this preflight.
